articleTitle: Comparison of Simple Moving Average, Single and Modified Single Exponential Smoothing
abstract: Various forecasting algorithms have been investigated in various cases. Forecasting is an important activity, especially in the sales area. Accurate sales forecasting is a support system in increasing company turnover. The single exponential smoothing algorithm is one of the most commonly used forecasting algorithms, but its weakness is that the value of is chosen at random, despite the fact that the value greatly influences the accuracy of forecasting results. The selection of the value can be done by applying an optimization algorithm, such as the particle swarm optimization algorithm. The accuracy of the forecasting system is compared using single exponential smoothing method, single exponential smoothing method optimized by particle swarm optimization, and simple moving average algorithm in this study to find out a better method in forecasting, so it can be a suggestion for a company that will build a forecasting system. Based on the accuracy tests carried out using the MAPE and RSME measures, the best forecasting results were discovered by utilizing the single exponential smoothing method which was optimized with particle swarm optimization with an RMSE value of 1,222,701 and a MAPE of 21.86 %.

articleTitle: Improving Stance-based Fake News Detection using BERT Model with Synonym Replacement and Random Swap Data Augmentation Technique
abstract: The amount of fake news on the internet remains to grow due to its low time and cost of publishing information. A fake news detection system can be implemented to combat its spread. In this research, a stance-based fake news detection model is built with a pretrained Bidirectional Encoder Representations of Transformers (BERT) model fine-tuned for stance detection between headline and body text with data augmentation. The data augmentation utilized in this research includes synonym replacement which replaces chosen words with their synonym, and random swap, which randomly replaces position between two words. The experiment is done by using the two data augmentation techniques separately, combining the two techniques where half of each augmentation is done by one technique, and mixing the two techniques. The evaluation on the test set by cross-validation shows that random swap augmentation provides the best result overall with 42.63% sensitivity, 82.14% specificity, 32.44 % Fl-score, with the least cost on accuracy with 71.52 % accuracy.

articleTitle: Electrical Parameter Analysis on DLP 3D Printers using IoT (Internet of Things)
abstract: In this research, we develop a current, power, energy, and voltage monitoring system which is implemented on a 3D printer. The printer used is a 3D DLP (Digital Light Processing) printer, where this printer uses a 3D photopolymer resin that can solidify under a light source. We added IoT (Internet of Things) technology to make it easier for users to monitor 3D printer usage. One of the additional components used is the ESP 32, which functions as the main processor for processing and sending data. The system is equipped with a PZEM-004T sensor to transmit current, power, energy, and voltage readings. System testing is done by printing objects in three-dimensional form, including factory shapes, circles, pluses, triangles, and squares. Based on the test results, it is found that the longest response time is when the system prints a box object, which is 110 minutes, while the fastest response time on the plus object is 24 minutes. This proves that sending data using ESP32 can be used to implement IoT technology.

articleTitle: Diagnose Pest and Disease of Black Orchid Plant Using Naive Bayes Method
abstract: Coelogyne pandurata or better known by Kalimantan Black Orchid. This plant is an epiphytic orchid that is attached to other plants but is not dangerous. This orchid is one of Kalimantan's endemic plants that require human intervention to save its sustainability. Black Orchid Plants are very susceptible to various pests and diseases; therefore, applications are needed that can provide insight to ornamental plant farmers. This study uses the Naive Bayes methods in the application of Expert Systems to diagnose pests and diseases of Black Orchid plants. There are 24 types of symptoms and nine types of diagnostic results. The results of this study are expected to provide a solution for cultivating Black Orchid plants so that they can find out the symptoms of pests and plant diseases early on. Nine diagnostic results consist of 4 types of pests and five types of disease. This application has a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) value of 2.456%.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis in Reviews About Beaches in Bali on Tripadvisor Using Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)
abstract: The tourism sector utilizes information and communication technology in promoting Indonesian tourism so tourists can obtain information about Indonesian tourism through websites, one of which is Tripadvisor. As one of the marine tourism spots in Indonesia, Bali uses the review from Tripadvisor web in developing, evaluating, and promoting its tourist attractions. However, there is a discrepancy between the rating and the review given by the user, and the review contains a paradoxical figure of speech in one review. This study is about a sentiment analysis on reviews of the five most favorite beaches in Bali: Double Six, Seminyak, Nusa Dua, Kelingking, and Canggu, using the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) in the Tripadvisor website. By approaching in 4 steps: preprocessing data (word stemming, lemmatization, data labeling, tokenization), TF-IDF weighting, classification using RNN, and performance evaluation. The result of sentiment analysis is that positive labels dominate. This study also calculated the value of precision, recall, F1-Score, and ROC curve for each beach. The accuracy gets more than 80%. ROC curve is classified as “Fair Classification” and “Good classification” with AUC values between 0.71-0.87. This proves that RNN has good performance and accuracy in performing sentiment analysis on reviews of the five most favorite beaches in Bali.

articleTitle: Acceptance of Virtual Campus Tour Using the TAM Approach: a Case Study in UPN Veteran Jawa Timur, Indonesia
abstract: Various policies regarding the application of information and communication technology are one form of effort to realize efficient and effective information delivery, one of the institutions or agencies that implement information and communication technology policies is an educational institution. When technology is developing, especially communication technology along with the presence of the COVID-19 Pandemic. In this regard, to provide the best information is also felt by the National Development University “Veteran” East Java in introducing the situation and condition of the campus by implementing a Virtual Campus Tour. The purpose of this study was to determine the factors that influence the acceptance of the virtual tour of UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) model. This study uses proportionate stratified random sampling with a total of 266 respondents who are active students at UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur. Based on the results of the analysis, it was found that the factors that influence user behavior in using the virtual tour of UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur on an ongoing basis are factors of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, attitude toward using, and usability with significant results on the intention to use the UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur virtual tour. While the factor that most influences the behavior of users to accept Virtual Tour of UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur is the usability factor, this is because usability has the largest path coefficient value, which is 0.714 compared to other variables.

articleTitle: An ensemble-of-classifiers approach for corn leaf based diseases detection
abstract: This study at hand proposes an ensemble-of-classifiers approach for corn leaf based diseases detection. Instead of using a single classical machine learning method, it developed a detection model by employing two classification methods: Voting Classifier with Majority Voting and 5 Classification and Regression Tree (CART) with max depth 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 to obtain higher accuracy in results. In particular, it benefited from PlantVillage, a public repository that provided over 8,000 corn leaf images as the dataset for the training and testing. All these images were extracted using the Global Color Histogram (GCH), Color Coherence Vector (CCV). Test results of segmented image against Red pixel using the Color Processing Detection Algorithm (CPDA) showed the best accuracy with a Precision of 82.92%, Recall 82.55%, and an f1-Score of 82.6%.

articleTitle: Design Transparent Microstrip Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting at 2.4 GHz
abstract: RF energy harvesting is an alternative method to power wireless networks. RF energy harvesting obtains a continuous electricity supply from the radio environment. In this paper, a transparent microstrip RF energy harvesting antenna to create cost-friendly smart energy technology is proposed. The material used is a transparent conductive AgHT-4 coated film printed on a 2 mm thick glass substrate. The antenna dimension is 47 mm x 35.5 mm. The transparent material for the antenna is chosen for a vehicle, building, or any on-glass surface application and will be used as a wireless communication antenna at a 2.4 GHz band while it also used for RF energy harvesting. The proposed antenna design is obtained through determining the initial layout of the antenna based on the formula, characterization, and modification of the antenna shape, then simulated using CST Microwave Studio to evaluate the antenna performance. The simulation results show transparent antenna has the lowest return loss of −38.644 dB at 2.401 GHz and a gain of 5.028 dBi.

articleTitle: Scheduling of Nurse's Work Shift of Emergency Room Unit using Goal Programming
abstract: The public health center, Puskesmas, is the front line representation of the City-Municipal Public Health Office responsible for providing public health services in a local region. Puskesmas usually has an emergency rooms service unit that serves the community 24 hours a day. It is necessary that the Emergency Room Unit formulate nurses' work shift schedules in order to deliver quality services for their patients. Most of the time, nurses' monthly shift rotations and schedules are carried out manually. The scheduling process often takes a long time, and the results have not been able to fulfill all the nurses' aspirations to carry out their duties in safe and sound working conditions. Therefore, this study aims to develop nurses' monthly work shift schedule that provides more balanced workloads using the Goal Programming method, and also, in each shift, there is at least one male nurse. The proposed scheduling model shows that all conditions required by the hospital can be fulfilled, and the variance due to the workloads of shifts and day-off among nurses can be minimized in order to support quality health services implementation.

articleTitle: Optimization Wire-EDM Parameters on Kerf Width and Involute Accuracy in Medium Carbon Stell using Grey Fuzzy Analytics and Fuzzy Logic
abstract: This research was conducted to simultaneously determine optimum parameters for meeting low kerf width and high involute accuracy on wire-EDM. Some gear is processed by wire-EDM to meet JIS B 1701:1973 series one standard. A defect on gear might have many consequences, from rejection on the production line to backlash phenomena in operation. This research aims to find the optimal parameters of wire-EDM to minimize those detriments. Taguchi methods and matrix orthogonal L18 were applied as research methods, while grey fuzzy analytics and fuzzy logic were used to identify optimum parameters. In this research, medium carbon steel DIN: 1.2378 was cut using Zinc-coated-brass wire. Variable on this research includes pulse-off time having two levels, while pulse-on time, open voltage, and wire feed has three levels. Methods used to optimize multi-response characteristics are grey relational analysis and fuzzy logic. This research can achieve responses that meet their quality characteristics by setting the process variables pulse-off time at 12µs, pulse-on time at 6 µs, the open voltage at 85 V, and wire feed at 10 mm/s. The result of involute accuracy on confirmation experiment is 1.6225mm and kerf width 0,333 µm. The highest research parameter contribution is the pulse on-time 70,33 %, and the lowest is wire feed 6,29%.

articleTitle: Integration System of IoT Gas Sensor using Simple Network Management Protocol and Open Platform Communication
abstract: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) has moved from being used only as a tool to monitor a network to becoming one of the standard data communication protocols. SNMP is supported by Open Platform Communication (OPC) and recent microcontrollers. Therefore, it can be used to integrate OPC and micro controllers. This paper aims to measure the SNMP performances such as data validity and latency during data communication. The SNMP protocol is implemented in the IoT sensor (MQ-6 gas sensor) integration system with the human-machine interface (HMI) via an OPC server. The MQ-6 sensor is integrated with the ESP32 micro controller as a tool for processing sensor data. The micro controller is then configured to become an SNMP Agent to communicate with the OPC Server, which acts as the SNMP Manager. Then, the OPC Server becomes the data center for several OPC Clients, including HMI and Prosys OPC Client as historians. The results show that the data was successfully sent and displayed on the HMI. The data transmitted using the SNMP protocol is validated with the data sent using a web-based protocol without SNMP. In testing duration for 30 minutes, the average latency was 17.7 ms without any data corruption or Request Time Out (RTO).

articleTitle: The Impact of Segment Length on EEG Based Biometric System
abstract: The biometric system is one of the best systems that can be used to replace the password system. Several modalities, such as fingerprints, face recognition, palm prints, and voice recognition, are reported to perform well as biometric modalities. Therefore, the current biometric system is still facing some issues. Artificial biometric data is the main issue in recent biometric systems. The electroencephalogram (EEG) signal is the potential modality to resolve the issue. Many studies have found that the EEG biometric system is able to achieve high accuracy. Most of them require a signal segmentation process to enrich the features and achieve high accuracy. In spite of that, there are only a few studies that focus on the impact of signal segmentation. In this study, 60, 30, 15, 10, 7.5, 6, 5 second lengths of segment were investigated. The power spectral density (PSD) feature from the delta (0.5 – 4 Hz), tetha (4 – 8 Hz), alpha (8 – 14 Hz), beta (14 – 30 Hz), and gamma (30 – 50 Hz) bands were extracted from each segment. It found that there was no linear correction between segment length and accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of Renewable Energy Sources for Rural Electrification at a Remote Outer Island
abstract: Many remote outer islands in Madura lack the electricity and high cost to connect them with the electrical grid from the government. However, the location has abundant renewable energy sources such as solar and wind energy, and it is suitable for installing dedicated renewable energy power systems for electrification. This study uses HOMER simulation software to simulate the solar-wind hybrid system to fulfill the electrical energy demand in the remote outer island. The solar-wind hybrid system provides 100% electrical energy with possible investment costs. The total initial capital from developing renewable power sources is estimated to be USD 4,02 million, USD 548,33 thousand, and USD 1,4 million for Massalima Island, Masakambing Island, and Karamian Island, respectively. The COE is $0,548 per kWh, and it is viable for electricity costs in the remote outer island. This COE can be reduced by utilizing excess electrical energy for heating and cooling purposes. It also improves the economic condition in rural areas.

articleTitle: pH Optimization in Pretreatment Process from Liquid Waste of Tapioca Flour with Response Surface Method
abstract: The starch content material contained in Liquid Waste of Tapioca Flour (LW-TF) may be processed into glucose via way of means of a hydrolysis process, which was previously carried out by a chemical pretreatment process. The purpose of this research is to find the optimization of pH in the pretreatment process with LW-TF and Hydrochloric acid (H-Cl) volume, the usage of software program with regression equation. The filtration process was carried out to remove impurities, the chemical pretreatment process used LW-TF with a variation of 200 to 1000 ml and a hydrolysis temperature of ± 40 OC, H-Cl variable 5 to 25 ml, and a stirring time of 30 minutes using MS-20D type digital magnetic stirrer. In the fermentation process the addition of Amylase enzyme as much as 11 %w/v and Maltose enzyme as much as 9%w/v to glucose contains 24.9 %v/v. Optimization of pH using Response Method Surface showing similarities to Regression Equation, obtained optimum pH of 8.85, Liquid Waste of Tapioca Flour volume of 1165.69 ml, and volume of H-Cl 0.859 ml, used as a reference for the next fermentation process to obtain optimum glucose levels.

articleTitle: ModelLStat: A Tool for Static Analysis in Model Layer on Web MVC Application
abstract: Model-View-Controller (MVC) is a design pattern that is commonly used for web applications. MVC divides applications into three main layers, the Model, the View Layer, and the Controller Layer. The model layer is related to the database. All data access to and from the database occurs at this layer. Usually, to monitor database activity, we use tools from database tools in the server. That tools allow us to see real-time database load performance. The disadvantage of real-time monitoring is that we can perform analysis when the application is running. Lack in the implementation process will be seen as a whole when the application is running. If errors are known when the program is running, the costs will be higher. Therefore, in this study, we create a tool to analyze the model layer. The analysis we use is static analysis. We try to analyze information from the code in the model layer. From the code in the model layer, we will analyze information on classes, functions, queries, and the frequency of tables are accessed in the database. With this static analysis, we can anticipate the access data within the application before the application goes live.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-programming-based Decision-making Support for Production Planning Problems in Excess Demand and Uncertain Prices in Recovery Time After a Pandemic
abstract: This paper provides decision-making support for solving raw part procurement problems in excess demand and fuzzy-uncertainty-based prices, suitable for use during the recovery time after a pandemic. The decision-making support model used a fuzzy programming-based mathematical model. Computational simulations with randomly generated data were used to demonstrate and evaluate the decision-making processes. The results showed that the model solved the given problems successfully i.e. the optimal volume for parts ordered to each supplier and the optimal lot of each product brand to be produced were derived optimally. This concludes that the proposed model can be used by managers in industries to solve their problems.

articleTitle: Classification of Online Learning Materials Using Artificial Intelligence

authors.preferredName: Mohd Nihra Haruzuan Bin Mohamad Said

abstract: In a new normal era, all teachers use online learning to teach their students. Each of the teachers makes the material in online learning, so it makes problems in online learning and students, there are many materials on the same topic and the same subjects that make useless and overlap in the material of teaching. The purpose of this research solves this problem. This research makes a system that can classify based on the topics and the subjects in online learning, so teachers do not make another material and became overload in database online learning. The system uses Artificial intelligence to classify the material based on topic and subject. The processing in classification use model of document classification. The processing has 2 processing that are modeling the training of document and classification documents based on the features of document. The system was tested in existing online learning and use 2 of testing the application to get accuracy and validation. The first testing is that the accuracy in this testing is check a functional of naive Bayes algorithm. This aim in this is to get accuracy, precision and recall in the algorithm. The second of test is that application is validated by validator to get valid or no valid about the result. All of testing given a significant average both testing in algorithm and testing in validation. The average of rate all testing is 83, 5% that this research success to classify the material on online learning based on specific subject

articleTitle: IoT-Based Portable Fingerprint Attendance System Using the Minutiae Based Algorithm
abstract: Attendance really needs to be done in order to know the attendance and time of arrival and return of someone from employees or workers to the education system. Attendance, which at first was only done manually, like signatures on paper, has now become more advanced, which is done using an electronic device using a fingerprint presence system. by using the concept of the internet of things which facilitates the online presence system through a network such as wi-fi, as well as portable or can also be carried everywhere. This portable IoT fingerprint presence system (PoFAS-Class) uses the Algortima Minutiae Based method where the algorithm detects lines or strokes on each human fingerprint. The components to help the success of the tool are the Nodemcu ESP8266 as a Microcontroller, Fingerprint Sensor, TFT OLED Screen, Battery Charger Module, and Web Information to register fingerprints and to inform users. Tool testing is done using a sample of 240 users who are registered into the presence information system, and the average processing time used to register a user's fingerprint on the sensor is < 5 seconds.

articleTitle: Short Term Prediction of Electrical Load Using Artificial Neural Network with Backpropagation Algorithm
abstract: Artificial neural network is one of the machine learning algorithms that can perform a regression or classification with supervised learning. In principle, artificial neural network has the same way of working as the system network in the human brain, which has the ability to learn from past experiences. In this paper, it will be proposed to design an artificial neural network model to be able to determine the amount of electrical load generated from a building in Telkom University for the next 7 days. The purpose of predicting this electrical load is to be able to plan of using electrical energy for the future. So that the waste from electrical energy can be minimized by making a prediction of the electrical load made from an artificial neural network model. Prediction of electrical load is done by predicting the last 7 days in January 2020 with training data for 24 days in the same month. The results of the research that has been done during weekend have a larger error than weekdays marked on the 26th has the largest error of 12.123% and the lowest error occurs on the 29th with an error value of 5.737%

articleTitle: Service Quality Analysis of M-Health Application Satisfaction And Continual Usage
abstract: Smartphone technology in health is critical, especially in improving health services quality and quality. The use of smartphone technology in health services is called Mobile Health (M-Health). The application of M-health is one solution to improve the quality of public health services. The application of M-Health will make it easier for users to obtain health information and services. JKN Mobile is an M-Health application that provides health insurance services managed by the Indonesian government. The JKN Mobile application has several features such as documentation of medical records, viewing the number of bills to be paid, updating participant data, and conducting online doctor consultations. This study aims to analyze the service quality factors that affect satisfaction and continuous use of the JKN Mobile Application using the Service Quality of M-Health Model. This study uses quantitative methods by analyzing data using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) involving 100 respondents using the JKN Mobile Application. The results showed that the variables of interaction quality and information quality as dimensions of service quality significantly influenced user satisfaction. Information quality has a significant influence on sustainable use. Monetary cost does not significantly affect user satisfaction and continuous use of the JKN Mobile Application.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Protocol Infrared System for Home Appliances
abstract: The development and research regarding the control system of household electronic equipment today have been widely done. The control system was developed based on infrared aimed at replacing various types of conventional remotes so that users only have one sophisticated remote that can control various types and brands of household electronic devices. However, the existing developments do not provide many changes to the control system of household electronic devices; significant changes are only about brands that can be supported by the system without providing other additional features. In this research, the design of a universal remote control system that can copy data and multi-protocols from conventional infrared remotes. This capability allows the remote control system to function as a conventional remote. This research was implemented on DVD and TV devices with several commonly used brands such as Asiatech, Sony, Polytron, Samsung, and Panasonic. The results obtained that from several brands tested, there are coding constraints and reading signal data on conventional Panasonic remotes on both DVD and TV devices. While in other brand electronic devices, the system can read and encode signals instead of conventional remotes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Streaming Video on VPN Networks Between OpenVPN and L2TP/IPSec
abstract: Advances in multimedia technology currently have a positive impact on its users. Users get information in the form of text, audio, images, and even video delivered through the streaming method, also known as video streaming. The problems encountered in video streaming are security, confidentiality, and authenticity when it comes to users and will be dangerous if misused by outside parties. VPN is needed as a form of protection against this. The simulation is carried out by sending video files with 360p, 480p, and 720p resolutions on L2TP networks with IPSec and OpenVPN. Data packets on the VPN network will be captured by Wireshark. The capture results will be calculated on the Quality of Service parameters, namely delay, jitter, throughput, packet loss, so that good quality of service can be obtained. After calculating the data on the two VPNs, Based on the parameters of delay, throughput, and packet loss in video streaming experiments, Open VPN is better than L2TP/IPSec. As for jitter parameters, L2TP/IPSec is better than Open VPN. Based on the QoS index, the index on L2TP/IPSec scored 2.5 in the unsatisfactory category. While the index on Open VPN scored 3.42 in the satisfactory category. By far, the advantage of Open VPN is that it allows secure user authentication for streaming video.

articleTitle: Identification of Acute Respiratory Infections in Toddlers Based on the Chi-Square And Naive Bayes Methods
abstract: Acute Respiratory Infections usually attack the respiratory tract of toddlers, both the upper and lower respiratory tracts, because the body's defense system against viruses that cause infection has not yet been formed. And usually, parents will know if the baby's condition is very chronic so that the baby experiences complications. This causes the need for a system that can assist in the early detection of respiratory tract infections. This study proposes the Chi-Square and Naive Bayes (NB) method. The Chi-Square method is a feature selection method to reduce features that have no effect. At the same time, the NB method is a prediction method that performs a simple probability-based identification process based on the application of the Bayes theorem with the assumption of strong independence. The contribution of this study is to determine respiratory tract disease in infants using the chi-square feature selection and the NB method, which can assist parents in detecting respiratory tract infections. From the tests that have been carried out using 120 datasets with 90 as training data and 30 as test data, the accuracy is 75.833%. This proves that the Chi-Square and NB methods are able to identify respiratory tract infections.

articleTitle: Classification of Proper or Improper Masks during a Pandemic Using a Custom Convolutional Neural Network with Data Augmentation
abstract: Classification of the use of masks today is very necessary regarding the pandemic period that is not over yet. This is mainly to break the chain of transmission of the COVID-19 virus from one person to another. From the literature that has been studied, the Convolutional neural network method can be used to distinguish the types of masks used in society. The advantage of the Convolutional Neural Network is that it can recognize objects with a fairly high level of accuracy, but it has a weakness, namely that the training process time is still quite high. This is the author's concern by doing a custom layer on the convolutional neural network. In addition, the addition of data augmentation is done to increase the number of data variations. The result used 18–34 custom layers in an average of around 97.93%, with an average computation time for the training process of about 1 minute 83 seconds. The resulting classification errors using Mean Absolute Error is 0,0163

articleTitle: Estimation Length of Study Period Using A Fuzzy Logic Model
abstract: Education is an essential part of forming quality and dignified human resources. Forming an intelligent and quality young generation is one of the roles of universities as one of the formal education providers. They are obliged to develop the best curriculum and encourage students to have competencies according to the chosen study program and graduate on time. However, there are many cases where not all students graduate on time and even drop out of school. The purpose of this research is to build a fuzzy logic model that can estimate the length of the study period so that universities can take preventive action against students who have the possibility of not graduating or dropping out or do not graduate on time. The contribution of this research is to build a model to estimate student learning time using a simplified fuzzy logic model. This simplified fuzzy logic model was proven to be able to estimate the length of learning. Initially, it consisted of 23 rules with an error rate of 11% and simplified to ten rules with 10.59%.

articleTitle: Application of Improved Random Forest Method and C4.5 Algorithm as Classifier to Ransomware Detection Based on the Frequency Appearance of API Calls
abstract: The signature base technique cannot recognize new types of Ransomware without first analyzing it. For that, we need a method to detect Ransomware using machine learning. This study aims to apply the improved Random Forest method to detect Ransomware in a random. The Forest used the feature evaluator and filter instances to increase the accuracy of the regular Random Forest. This study will use the improved Random Forest method with the C4.5 algorithm as a classifier to detect Ransomware. In this study, several stages were done to detect Malware using an improved Random Forest, namely extracting API calls, then selecting features based on the occurrence ratio of Malware, performing evaluator, resampling features, and then classifying them. The feature used API calls in the Malware based on the frequency that appears the most. Implementation of Ransomware detection using the improved Random Forest method obtained an accuracy value of 96% with an API call ratio value of 0.02 with 188 features. The results show that the Ransomware detection software is ineffective for all conditions. Because some Ransomware has not had the same API call, which affected failed the detection.

articleTitle: Auto-Image Colorization Of Grayscale Images Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: There are lots of old pictures in black-and-white and grayscale. When a grayscale image is painted, it can show the clarity of the past image. Many methods were proposed to perform a color transformation on greyscale images. Some include using manual methods and chemicals to more modern ones using graphic design software. However, all of these methods require special skills and a long time. We need a system that can automatically perform color transformations on gray images. The system developed in this study uses the Self-attention and Spectral Normalization GAN (SSN-GAN) algorithm, which automatically transforms grayscale images. This method was chosen because it can solve various image-to-image translation problems. This method produces a better initial score and a more stable training process. Self-attention is used to increase the initial score of the image generated by the GAN. The addition of spectral normalization makes the training process on the GAN run more stable. At the same time, by increasing the learning rate on the generator and discriminator, the model can produce a better image. In this study, researchers used two loss functions, namely, using SSIM Loss and without SSIM Loss. The highest accuracy value in the test with an epoch value of 50 and using SSIM loss, the accuracy value obtained is 59.9

articleTitle: Educational Application Development as an Effortless Solution for Basic Level Learning Media
abstract: Basic level learning media is an educational application intended for elementary school students as a distance learning media. With the pandemic, it has caused learning activities that were previously carried out directly to be transferred to distance learning. however, some learning management systems are still very complex and difficult to use. In this study, we developed an educational media application that was focused for learning basic level. The purpose of this research is that students can carry out learning activities using learning media independently. Steps being taken in the development of this application including problem identification, data collection and analysis, design, implementation and testing. To obtain complete data, data collection techniques by observing and distributing questionnaires were applied. Desktop-based application development using the Java language. Then perform the test by testing the applied black box and the results are obtained that the system being developed can run optimally on all features.

articleTitle: Geographic Information System (GIS) for Salt Management in Madura Island
abstract: Madura Island is known as Salt Island because it has many salt fields, produces a high volume of salt, and is the main contributor to national salt production. There are some salt fields in Sampang, Pamekasan, and Sumenep districts. It is essential to manage, control, improve, and decide Salt production in Madura island. There is still limited research about GIS for Salt Management for the case study in Madura Island. Therefore, this paper aims to capture and design a Geographic Information System (GIS) for Salt Management in Madura. The system will map salt fields, storage, production, marketing, and other places. Hopefully, it contributes by providing a GIS model for Salt mapping, management, and decision-making in Madura. The novelty of this research is the developed system based on the case study in Madura Island. This paper is developed based on progress research about GIS for Salt Management based on the Scrum model in Madura.

articleTitle: The Arrangement of Convolutional Neural Network Layers for Digit Speech Recognition
abstract: Digit Speech Recognition (DSR) is speech recognition based on the utterance of digit: one through nine. Itincluded isolated recognition (one word). The system begins with the digit as input data audio. Furthermore, the audio is converted into a digital signal and became a spectrogram whichis a 2-dimensional shape of the signal. The spectrogram is processed to obtain features using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). These features determine the results of recognition. The architecture that built for the system consists of a 24 layers: an input layer, five convolutional layers, five batch normalization, five Rectified Linear Units (ReLU), four max-pooling layers, dropouts, fully connected layers, softmax, and classification layers. Testing uses minibatch-size 64, learning rate 3e-4, max-epoch 25. Optimization uses Root Means SquarePropagation (RMSProp). The percentage data experiment consists of 60:20:20 for training, validation, and testing. The results showed precision, recall, and accuracy were 95.91%, 96.19%, 95.88% respectively.

articleTitle: User experience measurement on augmented reality mobile application for learning to read using a phonics-based approach
abstract: Reading skills in early childhood provide the foundation for acquiring and mastering other lessons that are useful for their lives. The use of fun interactive learning media is one technique to boost interest in reading for early childhood. The advantage of the phonics-based method that emphasizes word learning through the listening of letter sounds makes it easier for children to improve their reading skills. Augmented reality (AR) development is beneficial because it helps students pay more attention and raise passion by including them in the learning process. This study aimed to create an AR-based multimedia application for learning to read by utilizing the phonics-based method, which is beneficial for the first step in advancing the reading skills of the Indonesian language. At the final stage of the study, a user experience measurement was conducted to investigate the level of acceptance of the developed application. The application that has been developed has been experimentally confirmed to have a high level of user acceptability.

articleTitle: Literature Review: Evolution Strategies Application in Solving Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: Evolution Strategies (ES) is a heuristic-nature-inspired algorithm that uses real-coded gene representation. It is in the same family of evolutionary algorithms as the Genetic Algorithm (GA). ES is less popular and rarely used in solving problems than GA, but some research has proved that ES can result in a feasible solution, sometimes better than GA. This literature review tries to review ES's performance in computational time and its ability. Multi-objective optimization (MO) cases. While the basic forms of ES such as (µ,λ)-ES, (µ/p, λ)-ES, (µ+ λ)-ES, and (µ/p+ λ)-ES is usually capable of solving complex problems, sometimes ES needs to be modified. Another modification has been made by making a hybrid algorithm between ES and Fuzzy Inference System (FIS). The 12 literature that has been reviewed proves that ES is indeed capable of solving multi-objective problems ranging from the ordinary to the very complex.

articleTitle: The Relationships between Aspects of Playability and Learning Content in Educational Games
abstract: The use of games as educational tools is becoming prevalent in and out of classrooms. Among the success factors of educational games is playability, which has been studied but only in general and high-level manners. This study tries to delve deeper into educational game playability by investigating its relationships with aspects of learning content. We experimented with an educational game whose learning content consisted of lessons belonging to three topics. The topics were related to informatics and differed in familiarity, comprehensibility, and memorability aspects. The game's playability consisted of five aspects: learnability, user interfaces, in-game goals, information presentation, and control scheme. The game was playtested by first-year informatics students, who afterward reported their playing and learning experiences through a questionnaire. We then conducted correlation tests and analysis on the questionnaire responses, which resulted in several interesting findings. Among the findings are (1) optimum playability is achieved when the three learning content aspects are satisfied, and (2) assuring the learnability aspect is crucial to the player's learning process. Lastly, we combine the findings from the correlation analysis and the players' critiques and suggestions to propose general principles for optimum playability in educational games.

articleTitle: The Acceptance of Technology in Agriculture: case in Dalangan Village
abstract: Dalangan Village in Sukoharjo Regency has designated a national experimental area for agricultural machinery and information technology implementation in farming activities since 2018. Because of its use in the domain, individuals unfamiliar with using digital technology and a lack of information so many are still hesitant to utilize it. The purpose of this study was to determine the factors that influence public acceptance of the innovation of agricultural machinery in Dalangan Village using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2). This research method is quantitative with an explanative research type. Data collection using a questionnaire with a survey method. The Partial Least Square (PLS) method with the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) model in the smart-PLS three applications for data processing. The results of this study indicate that of the 130 respondents, there are 25 people (19%) who never used the technology of agricultural mechanization tools and machines, 16 people (12%) used it, 38 people (29%) sometimes use it, 41 people (32%) frequently use. Then people (8%) very often use agricultural mechanization technology and machinery. Factors that significantly influence public acceptance of the use of agricultural machinery innovation are performance expectations, facilitating conditions, habits, and behavioral intention.

articleTitle: Value at Risk with Bootstrap Historical Simulation Approach for Prediction of Cryptocurrency Investment Risk
abstract: In the era of the digital economy, cryptocurrency has emerged as a new transaction tool and investment asset that is widely used by people all over the world. Cryptocurrencies are preferred because their security and privacy are guaranteed, and can provide greater profit potential than conventional financial investment assets (stocks, bonds, etc.). Although it can provide the possibility of higher returns, investing in cryptocurrencies does not mean that it is risk-free. Therefore, we need to know the estimated risk of loss that will occur to prepare a strategy so that the investment does not go bankrupt. This article aims to calculate predicted losses in the Top 5 Cryptocurrencies (as of June 2021) using VaR with the Bootstrap Historical Simulation approach. Using historical cryptocurrencies data from 01/07/2019-16/07/2021, at a 95% confidence level and a holding period of 1 day, the cryptocurrency with the highest risk of loss is Cardano (ADA), with a VaR value of 8.62%.

articleTitle: Building Enterprise Architecture for Future Service Station
abstract: Nowadays, several businesses use Enterprise Architecture (EA) to plan execution of projects. A service station of Thailand is a complex business comprising related vehicle services and other sub-businesses, perhaps including a petrol station, an engine oil and spare parts shop, a vehicle repair services, and a motel. A service station is a case study of this research. The authors studied the concepts to choose an appropriate EA framework. The authors determined a representative sample group: managers chosen from 252 service stations from the top 6 gasoline brands. Questionnaires were designed and distributed were used to assess the threshold range. The total accepted criteria scores can specify an appropriate EA framework. The authors designed and offered the EA service station framework as a template by combining the concepts of EA with digital transformation. The composition of a new service station EA framework was therefore developed as a guideline based on the architectural composition of the EA framework. Also, this new EA can be applied to future work.

articleTitle: Implementation Analysis of KEBI Application on Non-Standard Words Detection in Student Essay Tasks on Language Variety
abstract: Non-standard word errors in writing sometimes escape the attention of writers or editors due to several factors, including unintentional or limited time in editing. Non-standard word is one of the Indonesian spelling error. Therefore, the application for detecting non-standard words in writing, KEBI, was created to minimize the height of non-standard words in writing. In this study, KEBI was analyzed in terms of application implementation to five various language essay documents as student assignments for Indonesian language courses. There are three things that are analyzed, namely the interface page, processing time, and the level of accuracy of detection and correction using the precision and recall method (confusion matrix). The overall research method includes literature study, data collection, testing, measurement of display, time, and accuracy. Based on the results of the analysis, the interface page display shows good quality. The processing time required by KEBI to detect non-standard words is in the range of 0.02-0.06 seconds. Meanwhile, KEBI's non-standard word detection accuracy rate is 86%, while KEBI's non-standard word correction accuracy rate is 90%.

articleTitle: The Role of Complaint Application Evaluation in Knowledge Management Implementation for Organization Improvement: Text Processing Case Study in Directorate General of Treasury
abstract: In knowledge management, organizations have an important role in improving quality in various sectors. Evaluation is necessary to measure the effectiveness and efficiency of knowledge management in supporting organizational objectives. One form of the evaluation process used by government organizations is an internal evaluation by utilizing information on complaints from service users. Text processing is one method for mining datasets from government data complaints. Text processing results can be used as an analysis to conduct internal evaluations of the implementation of knowledge management. XGBoost algorithm is an alternative in processing text to produce a classification of data used as an analysis process. This study aims to determine the role of evaluating complaint texts during the implementation of knowledge management by studying cases of processing user complaint texts at the Directorate General of Treasury. SAKTI application is the main focus of the evaluation because as many as 65% of user complaint tickets are related to the SAKTI application. Based on the analysis, user understanding of SAKTI implementation and reporting tends to be poor. As a result of the research, some findings and discussions are given at the end of this article to achieve effective and efficient organizational knowledge management in general.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Application To Detect Face Masks For Health Protocol Surveillance During The Covid-19 Pandemic
abstract: As part of preventing the rapid spread of the COVID-19 virus, masks should be used besides physical distancing, avoiding crowds, setting good ventilation, cleaning hands, and more. In fact, there are still many people who do not use masks in public places. Security officers usually carry out the supervision system for the use of masks in public places. Direct interaction between security officers and many visitors in the long term will trigger a high risk of being infected. It is better if there is a system that can monitor the use of masks automatically and continuously. In this study, a deep learning algorithm with YOLOv3 architecture is applied to a web-based mask detection system. YOLOv3 is one of the best algorithms that has been widely applied and optimized by researchers for object detection. This system has been tested in two scenarios using different data sets, namely without augmentation and with augmentation. For each scenario, three experiments were carried out using varying amounts of training data, namely 10, 100, and 800. The best mAP and confidence values were obtained from experiments using 800 training data with augmentation. This mAP value is 0.99 with a confidence value range between 0.9 to 1.

articleTitle: Simulation Model of Vannamei Shrimp Cultivation System Using the Agent Based Modeling Approach
abstract: Fisheries cultivation is very potential in Indonesia because Indonesia has a large maritime area. Shrimp is a marine resource that has high economic potential with market demand. By looking at the high demand for exports and a fairly high selling price, Vannamei shrimp have the greatest potential to increase their cultivation yields. Several problems are still encountered in cultivating Vannamei in Socah Village. One of them is the difference in the conduct of each fish farmer in the cultivation process. For that, it is necessary to identify related interactions between fish farmers so that there is no gap in income and yields among them. This study performed Vannamei cultivation simulation modeling with an Agent-Based Model. The software used as a tool in ABMS simulation is NetLogo 6.0.4. In the real system, the income of the fish farmers is Rp. 31,385,000, while the simulation output is Rp. 31,385,230, with a difference of Rp. 230, which is of very small value and does not differ significantly. The best scenario results are using SPF (specific pathogen-free) certified shrimp seeds and adding 20% shrimp feed with Rp income. 37,908,030.

articleTitle: Green Technology E-toll Card: Level of acceptance and use of a technology
abstract: This study aimed to measure the level of acceptance and use of e-toll card technology. Respondents in this study were e-toll card users in four metropolitan cities in Indonesia, such as Bandung, Jakarta, Semarang, and Surabaya. The analysis method used was Structural Equation Model (SEM). This study indicated that perceived usefulness affected the attitudes of E- Toll Card usage. Perceived usefulness and Subjective Norm did not affect the intention to use e-toll cards. Perceived ease of use affected the perceived benefit of e toll card users. Perceived Behavioral Control and Attitude e toll card users affected the Intention To Use of e toll card users. The toll road manager immediately conveys the information regarding the e toll card related to the use and redeployment. Customers are given a choice of e-toll cards from all participating banks when bidding to customers. The toll road manager guarantees the receipt printer for every transaction made by the e-toll card user. The government guarantees toll road users no difficulties refilling e toll cards to support the non-cash national movement.

articleTitle: Applying Social Software for BPM Life Cycle: Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The use of social software in BPM helps to overcome the problems of traditional BPM through the controlled engagement of external stakeholders to improve organizational performance. There are many types of social software, such as tags, social links, recommendation and reputation systems, blogs, and wikis. On the other hand, various literature states that social software in BPM is beneficial for organizations. However, the types of organizations that benefit from social software have not been investigated. In this paper, we conduct a systematic literature review to determine the use of social software in BPM and its implementation in specific organizations. The results of our structured literature review show that the implementation of social BPM is most widely used in types of organizations such as SMEs and Education, as well as large enterprises and non-profit organizations. The type of social software in BPM that is widely used is the social link. However, there is no evidence of the use of blogs yet. The implementation of social software in BPM is discussed further. The results of this paper can be used to guide for planning the implementation social software in BPM in future research.

articleTitle: Kohonen-SOM LOF Approach for Anomaly Detection
abstract: Water loss in distribution is a serious problem for water companies, as it can result in a loss of profit. Machine learning has a method for dealing with this, for example, anomaly detection. Anomalies in the study were detected using data from March 2017 to February 2018. The data used is water consumption, and the variables such as mean water use, maximum water use, and standard deviation of water usage were obtained. Kohonen Self-Organizing Map (SOM) and Local Outlier Factor (LOF) are used because they can create a good cluster, and LOF can detect which one of them is filled with anomalies. The Kohonen SOM algorithm produced 45 groups that were considered anomalous because their silhouette width criteria were less than the group's average silhouette width. There are 45 different groups of unexpected anomalies. The LOF generated 1229 unusual consumption events, with each incident involving 579 households or customers. The frequency calculation yields 41 customers who are suspected of being anomalous. While the baseline method from the company only captures 16 anomalies out of 41 customers. This is because the company method fails to capture unusual consumption behaviors, such as monthly consumption. The anomaly detected the customer's characteristic of having an average of more than average usage of classes and sub-zones.
